assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and realised with strontium by Katori and Ye, are a clear invention that moved timekeeping to the 10^-18 regime. The discovery is concrete and has already enabled relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants.
assessment.attribution: The credited pair matches the two groups that drove the concept and its demonstration. Other contributors to lattice-clock physics (for example the theoretical magic-wavelength idea and ytterbium work) exist, but the supplied credit gives a clean two-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation by many laboratories worldwide and stable performance records over more than a decade make the recognition timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would weigh single-ion clocks and frequency-comb contributions as overlapping with earlier prizes.
The precise split of credit between the original proposal and the experimental realisation is from my general knowledge, not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new field of twistronics: a theoretical prediction of flat bands at a specific angle followed by experimental observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity. It is original, clear and has had broad impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery. A theory-plus-experiment trio is natural, though Cao and others in the experimental team, and parallel contributions on moire physics, may complicate allocation; only the supplied names can be used.
assessment.maturity: Independent replication across many groups, including scanning-probe and TEM-based structural characterisation, supports the physics, but the interpretation of the correlated phases is still evolving, so the timing is somewhat early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains debated.
Extreme sensitivity to sample quality and twist-angle disorder raises questions about which observations are intrinsic.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Negative-index and structured metamaterials, with the transformation-optics and perfect-lens ideas, reshaped optics and electromagnetism and led to engineered cloaking and flat-optics concepts. The discovery is original and widely recognised in physics and engineering.
assessment.attribution: Pendry supplied the decisive theoretical constructs (wire and split-ring media, perfect lens) and Smith the first experimental realisation of negative index. Capasso is credited for metasurfaces, a related but distinct development, so a Pendry-Smith pair is the cleaner configuration.
assessment.maturity: The field is mature with extensive confirmation, though practical impact of the original negative-index goals has been more limited than the early claims; recognition would not be premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the lasting scientific impact as mainly engineering rather than a fundamental discovery.
Priority questions around earlier work on negative refraction (Veselago) and the role of other experimental groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal for trapped-ion quantum computation by Cirac and Zoller and its experimental realisation by Blatt and others established a leading quantum-computing platform. The proposal-plus-implementation structure is clear.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller made the original gate proposal and Blatt's group demonstrated its key elements; this fits a three-person prize. Wineland and Monroe have contributions, and the prior prize to Wineland may bear on the scope.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of confirmation and now commercial-scale systems make this mature, though a recent related prize in quantum circuits could affect timing.
uncertainties: Overlap with B008 and B047 where the same three or four names appear, and whether the committee would split the field.
Overlap with the earlier Haroche-Wineland prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Solid-state femtosecond lasers (Ti:sapphire gain medium, Kerr-lens mode-locking, SESAMs) turned ultrafast science into a routine tool and underpin attosecond science, as recognised in the 2023 prize I chaired. The lasting impact is huge and the invention is clear.
assessment.attribution: Moulton for the Ti:sapphire laser, Sibbett's group for Kerr-lens mode-locking, Keller for semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors. Three people can be named, but each contribution is distinct and ordering of priority needs scrutiny.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with decades of use; the main issue is that parts of the enabling chain were already recognised, namely chirped pulse amplification in 2018 and attosecond pulses in 2023.
uncertainties: Whether recognition is felt as adjacent to recently prized ultrafast work.
The correct priority of Kerr-lens mode-locking among several groups in the early 1990s.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators, from the quantum spin Hall prediction to the first observation in HgTe and the quantum anomalous Hall effect, form a central chapter of condensed matter physics. The scientific significance is very high.
assessment.attribution: Kane provided key theory, Molenkamp the experimental quantum spin Hall observation, and Xue the quantum anomalous Hall effect. Missing from this configuration are Mele, Bernevig, Zhang and Hasan, so the allocation of credit is contested; B045 offers a different grouping.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed but the topology prize in 2016 already recognised related ideas, and the compound discovery has parts at different stages of maturity.
uncertainties: Unresolved credit between theorists and experimentalists, and the passing of Shoucheng Zhang as a relevant factor in fairness considerations.
Overlap with the duplicate topological-insulator candidate B045.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The qPlus sensor and CO-tip atomic force microscopy brought real-space imaging of molecular bonds and charge states. As a microscopist I value the instrumental invention and its demonstrated power, a recognised route to atomic-scale resolution on surfaces.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl invented the qPlus sensor, while Gross and Meyer at IBM Zurich demonstrated the bond-resolved imaging with functionalised tips. This is a plausible three-person split, though Binnig-Quate-Gerber earlier AFM work and other groups complicate priority.
assessment.maturity: Widely adopted in surface science and confirmed by many groups, though the field is narrower than competing candidates and the impact on physics as a whole may be considered smaller.
uncertainties: Whether the breadth of impact compares with larger fields on the longlist.
Interpretation of image contrast (for example bond-order versus tip relaxation) has been discussed in the literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Baryon acoustic oscillations provide a standard ruler that has fixed cosmological distances and constrained dark energy; the detection in galaxy surveys was a clean and important measurement.
assessment.attribution: Eisenstein and collaborators in SDSS and Cole, Peacock and others in 2dFGRS made independent detections in 2005. The supplied credit is plausible but the team nature of both surveys makes a three-person selection difficult.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by multiple surveys, though the interpretation within the cosmological model is still being tested against recent tension results; as an observational field it is outside my own expertise.
uncertainties: Team-based surveys make individual attribution hard.
My assessment relies on general knowledge, outside my own experimental area.
